meta.title: Kalman filter vs moving average
meta.tools: NumPy Kalman filter, discrete algebraic Riccati equation (SciPy) for the prediction
meta.summary: Track a manoeuvring 1-D target from noisy position measurements with a constant-velocity Kalman filter; predict the steady-state error from the Riccati equation and compare with the measured RMSE and with a moving average of the best length.
meta.problem: How much better than simple averaging can a model-based estimator do, and can its accuracy be predicted before running it?
meta.theory:
State $[p, v]$, $F=\begin{bmatrix}1&T\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$, white-acceleration process noise
$Q=q\begin{bmatrix}T^3/3&T^2/2\\T^2/2&T\end{bmatrix}$, measurement $H=[1\ 0]$ with variance r.
The steady-state *prior* covariance P solves the DARE $P=FPF^T-FPH^T(HPH^T+r)^{-1}HPF^T+Q$; the posterior
position variance is $P_{11}-P_{11}^2/(P_{11}+r)$ — its square root is the predicted RMSE. A moving average of
length M has noise variance r/M plus a lag bias growing with velocity and M.
meta.method:
T = 0.1 s, true motion simulated from the same model (q = 0.5 m²/s³), r = 4 m² (σ = 2 m), 20,000 steps. Kalman
RMSE vs the DARE prediction; moving averages M = 1…60, best M; also a model-mismatch run (true q ×10).

metrics.quantity: Accuracy gain over the best moving average

metrics.note: vs 0.97 m if the filter knew q
